perspective:
From Keith Ndiaye’s available perspective:

- Keith works as a construction worker at the same construction company where Elizabeth Sun is the receptionist. They are colleagues with a friendly but professional relationship, interacting when Keith comes to the office for paperwork and project updates.
- Recently, Keith observed Elizabeth being unusually curt/short with him over several days. He wondered if he had upset her, possibly through a misunderstanding or an unknown mistake.
- Keith asked Elizabeth directly whether he had done something to upset her. Elizabeth said no, that she was dealing with personal stuff, and apologized if she had seemed short.
- Keith felt sympathetic and offered to listen or take a coffee break. Elizabeth accepted and thanked him.
- During the coffee break, Elizabeth shared more about her stresses, which Keith perceived as quite severe. Keith told her he appreciated her sharing, then asked if she had considered talking to a professional. Elizabeth said she had thought about it but was unsure and hesitant about seeking help.
- Afterward, Keith noticed Elizabeth become slightly withdrawn. He worried that his suggestion might have embarrassed her or overstepped. He checked in, saying he hoped he hadn’t overstepped and that he was there to support her. Elizabeth said he hadn’t overstepped, appreciated his concern, and said it was a lot to think about.
- Later, Keith observed Elizabeth seeming more open and appreciative of his concern. He told her he was glad they could talk and that he is always available to chat or take breaks together. Elizabeth thanked him and said it meant a lot; she felt better knowing she had his support.
- Keith now believes Elizabeth values his support and feels more comfortable around him, and he intends to maintain this supportive relationship.
- Keith does not have access to hidden causes, private thoughts, or details Elizabeth did not state or show him.
